deviations.what: Add fade-in/fade-out and cross-fades (not in spec or plan). Govee has no native transition parameter, so govee-cli ramps client-side over LAN (steps every ~100-250 ms). (1) govee serve runs fades when it is running (approved d4: serve owns the lamp); any new command for that device cancels the running fade; without serve the CLI runs the fade in the foreground and Ctrl-C stops it. (2) 'govee light on/off' fade by default over a configurable default (1.5 s; GOVEE_FADE_DEFAULT, --fade 0 snaps); brightness/color/temp are instant unless --fade/fade_seconds is given. (3) Fades transition brightness, color and color temperature (cross-fade from current to target). Fade-in: set brightness 1, turn on, ramp up; fade-out: ramp down, turn off, remember the pre-fade brightness. LAN-only: over cloud (rate-limited) a fade degrades to an instant change with a warning. One event per fade; dry run shows the step plan; max 3600 s. New work: fade engine govee_cli/govee/fade.py + LampService hook (after t7 merges, before t8/t9/t10, parallel with t11); --fade on CLI (t8), fade_seconds on MCP set_light (t9), fade in web API + a duration control in the console (t10 + static UI), lamp_fade_on/lamp_fade_off {seconds} in the culture-rules actor (t12), tests in t13, real-lamp check in t14 (incl. whether the firmware adds its own short smoothing)
deviations.reason: User: fade-in and fade-out are critical for working with the lamp (2026-10-29); design choices answered by the user: serve runs fades, on/off fade by default, brightness+color+temp. Govee LAN/cloud APIs expose no transition time (developer forum request; community drivers step client-side).
